subject: Competitive bake-off recap and next steps — NovaNet
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Alvarez <sofia@novanet.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@novanet.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 05 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Competitive bake-off recap and next steps — NovaNet

Hi Sofia / Tom —

Thanks again for taking time today to walk through your use case and the bake-off plan. Below is a quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned.

Summary of pain points (what you told us)
- High inference cost at scale: current per-token costs are driving up margins for customer-facing features.
- Unpredictable latency for long conversations (3-5s p95 on existing infra) impacting UX.
- Data residency & audit requirements: logs/audit trails must remain in-region for pilot customers.

Goals for the pilot/bake-off
1) Validate throughput at 100 concurrent sessions with p95 latency < 750ms for typical 512-token prompts.
2) Demonstrate 2x cost improvement compared to current provider for production-like load.
3) Verify data residency, key management, and audit logging meet NovaNet security checklist.

Decision criteria (ranking you shared)
1) Latency stability (weighted)
2) Cost per 1M tokens
3) Security & compliance (in-region data + KMS)
4) Operational maturity (observability, fallbacks)

Open questions we captured
- Which specific regions must audit logs remain in for the pilot? (E.g., us-east-1 only or multi-region?)
- Procurement timeline / PO process and any required contract language (NDA already in place).
- Will you want a cloud-marketplace purchase or a standard purchase order?

Follow-up tests / PoC plan (proposed)
- Week 1: Initial technical setup — private trial environment with VPC peering and KMS test keys.
- Week 2: Controlled load test — 100 concurrent sessions with synthetic traffic; we’ll provide the test harness.
- Week 3: Customer-driven UX test — your product integrations with real conversations.
- Final: Delivery of bake-off matrix and cost/latency report.

Attachments included: redwood-bakeoff-matrix.xlsx (vendor comparison matrix), demo-recording.mp4 (screen recording of today’s demo).

Proposed next steps (please confirm)
- Sofia/Tom: confirm audit log region(s) and whether procurement wants marketplace or PO by EOD Friday.
- We (Marissa / Aditya / Vivek): set up VPC trial and share test runner by Monday 10 May.
- Book 60-min follow-up: 11 May preferred — I can send an invite once you confirm the time.

Thanks — looking forward to working together on this.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123
Redwood Inference

Attachment: demo-recording.mp4 (video/mp4)

From: Sofia Alvarez <sofia@novanet.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@novanet.com>
Date: Thu, 06 May 2027 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap and next steps — NovaNet

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. This aligns with what we discussed. A couple quick clarifications:

1) Audit log region: for the pilot we need logs to remain in us-east-1 only.
2) Procurement: we prefer to purchase via our marketplace contract if Redwood supports it; otherwise we will follow the PO route. I’ll confirm by Friday.
3) Latency targets: can you confirm whether the 750ms p95 target assumes an encoder/decoder model or decoder-only? Our current infra is decoder-only and we want an apples-to-apples comparison.

I’m looping in Tom on procurement specifics. Also please include our security lead (cc if you have a contact) when you share the KMS setup details.

Appreciate it — Sofia
Sofia Alvarez
Head of Product, NovaNet
sofia@novanet.com

Great — thanks Sofia. Quick answers and updates below, and I’ve attached an updated matrix that calls out model architecture assumptions.

- Region: confirmed — we’ll keep audit logs in us-east-1 for the pilot.
- Procurement: we support marketplace purchases; I’ve added marketplace and PO options in the attached matrix.
- Latency target: 750ms p95 assumes a decoder-only inference path (512-token typical prompt). We included both decoder-only and encoder-decoder columns in the matrix for clarity.

Next steps we’ll take today
- Aditya and I will start VPC/KMS setup and share the network playbook (Vivek will send the KMS integration steps).
- I’ll update the test harness to ensure the runner uses decoder-only model configs for the baseline comparison.
- Can you confirm by EOD if procurement wants marketplace or PO so we can finalize timeline?

Proposed follow-up: I’ll send a calendar invite for Tues 11 May 10:00 AM PT — please let me know if that works.

Thanks again — looped in Aditya and Vivek for visibility.

Best,

Marissa
